thread:
samir: Quick heads-up — I need an RBAC tweak for the private/VPC deploys tomorrow morning. Goal: restrict the model-pull service account so it cannot call the keystore API directly. Want audit flow and KMS signoff before we flip it.
elaine: Sounds prudent. Is this the change that removes iam:Decrypt from the cluster service principal?
samir: yes, we plan to remove Decrypt and add a dedicated short-lived signer role for model pulls. The signer will call KMS:Sign only, and we will validate via attestation.
jordan: How do we plan to record the key usage in audit logs? We need immutable chain for forensics if anything goes sideways.
samir: plan is: KMS usage -> KMS audit (cloud provider) + forward events to sec-sink (splunk) via TLS syslog; also mirror minimal event to local node logs for correlation.
amanda: can we ensure those mirrored logs are append-only and have integrity? We should checksum batches (sha256) and ship to S3 cold storage with object lock enabled.
samir: yes — object-lock retention for 90d is the plan for now. Also adding HMAC per-batch, stored in vault.
sec-bot: [automated] Note: existing audit-forwarder config uses port 6514/tls and rotates client cert every 7 days.
elaine: network policy question — model-pull nodes are in a shared subnet. We need to ensure they cannot egress to control-plane management endpoints except the KMS endpoint and the container registry. Any suggestions for netpol?
jordan: Use a default-deny egress on the pod level, then allow FQDN/IP ranges for registry + KMS + monitoring egress (Datadog). Be careful with FQDN rules — CDN IPs change. We use egress-proxy for registry to keep IPs stable.
amanda: For on-prem installs without egress-proxy, we should bind to a jumpbox NAT with strict host-based firewall rules + TLS inspection bypass exceptions for KMS.
samir: Good point. Also adding kube-netpol plus host firewall at node-level (nftables) for defense-in-depth.
ops-oncall: If we block Decrypt, what happens during incident when we need to rehydrate models quickly? Can the signer role be escalated temporarily?
samir: We will implement a canary path: an emergency runbook allowing temporary grant of KMS:Decrypt to a short-lived emergency principal, gated by two-person approval and recorded in the audit trail. Also auto-expire after 1h.
jordan: Vulnerability triage: yesterday's SBOM scan flagged an old libcurl CVE on edge-image fetcher. Is this related? If exploit exists, could an attacker get a model artifact that points to a malicious image which calls our keystore?
elaine: attack path low because container runtime restricts capabilities, and model-pull runs with read-only rootfs. But we should patch the image and rotate signatures.
amanda: reminder: signed image verification at admission controller is turned on for private installs?
sec-bot: [automated] Admission policy: image signature verification = ON for prod-private clusters, WARN for staging.
samir: We'll schedule image rebuilds and a signature rotation. Also adding additional admission check: block images pulled from registries not in allowlist.
devops: For RBAC rollout, advise canary in a sandbox tenant first. Test audit-forwarder under load to ensure no event loss (we saw 0.2% drop last q under burst).
samir: agreed. Plan: 1) sandbox canary tomorrow 09:00 2) run audit-forwarder stress test 3) validate KMS signer workflow and emergency grant 4) escalate to prod change window after signoff.
elaine: I'll own the audit/splunk validation and object-lock setup.
jordan: I'll validate netpol/nftables config on a host and draft the emergency grant runbook.
amanda: I'll patch the edge-image and rebuild signatures.
ops-oncall: I'll monitor the canary and be on-call for rollback.
samir: thanks everyone. tagging @here in case compliance wants to review before prod. :eyes:
amanda: @compliance-team if you can peek at the object-lock retention and emergency grant text, that'd be great.
sec-bot: [automated] Incident playbook link: https://intra.redwood/ops/playbooks/kms-emergency.
samir: iterative note — add a correlation-id header (X-RDW-AUDIT-ID) from the signer to the KMS request so we can join traces across systems.
elaine: +1, makes triage easier. Also ensure log timestamps are in UTC ISO8601 and synced (chrony).
jordan: final Q — do we need per-tenant KMS keys for cryptographic isolation or is signer-per-tenant orthogonal?
samir: long term per-tenant keys ideal, but for this rollout we'll do signer-per-tenant principal mapping to a shared key with strict access controls. roadmap item: migrate to per-tenant CMKs next quarter.
amanda: ok. I'll add the SBOM CVE mitigation to the release notes.
ops-oncall: rolling plan looks good. please paste the canary command and netpol rules once ready.
samir: will do, posting follow-up thread with diffs and rollback commands after the sandbox run. :white_check_mark:
